item.title: DL Gabriel Truss survived severe car accident to earn second chance at college football
item.description: Garden City Community College defensive lineman Gabriel Truss committed to Eastern Michigan this weekend. The Eagles have a good class of JUCO additions coming in, but Truss is a little different. He is a 6-foot-3, 320-pound run stuffer who has college experience having played at Missouri Western State prior to coming to Garden City. What makes him extra unique are the circumstances that brought him to Garden City and have made him so appreciative of every day he gets to play football and simply be alive. “I got in a car accident and thought I’d never play football again,” Truss said. “I had split my jaw almost in half, I was missing my bottom four teeth, I fractured the top of my spine, broke my leg, fractured rib, I had a concussion, and had emergency jaw surgery.” The early days in the hospital were tough. “There were days when I was in terrible pain,” Truss said. “I’d be in my hospital bed, pressing my button and waiting for the nurse to come bring me pills to take away the pain and I tried not to question why God put me through this. But my faith played a big factor. I’m so thankful now for getting offers to play at the next level.” Eastern Michigan proved to be that right opportunity, with his official visit to Ypsilanti sealing the deal for Truss. “I would say the coaches, their hospitality, and their interest in me made me want to be there. And I liked the facilities, the meeting rooms and all that,” Truss said. With that, Truss now prepares for the next step of his journey, which is enrolling mid-year at Eastern Michigan. “Getting this opportunity, coming from where I’m from and being through what I’ve been through, I just am very thankful,” Truss said. Truss had 16 tackles (2.5 for loss) this season for Garden City.

item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo Ruled Out for Heat’s Showdown Against Thunder
item.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images The Miami Heat will be missing a crucial piece of their lineup as they prepare to face the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday. Star forward Giannis Antetokounmpo has been ruled out due to a groin injury, marking his first missed game since joining the Heat in the offseason. Antetokounmpo, a former two-time MVP, has been instrumental in Miami’s early success this season, averaging an impressive 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 1.3 blocks while shooting 60.2% from the field across 15 games. His absence will undoubtedly be felt as the Heat look to maintain their momentum. The Thunder, too, will be without star power, as reigning two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is sidelined with a lower back contusion and neck strain. Both players were initially listed as questionable, but the decision to keep them out comes as both teams navigate through the challenges of the season. Miami is speculated to look to Bobby Portis Jr. to step into the starting lineup in place of Antetokounmpo. Portis brings energy and experience, but replacing the production and leadership of Giannis will be a tall order for the Heat. As the Heat entered Sunday with a record of 9-6, sitting in sixth place in the Eastern Conference, the team is keen to capitalize on their home court advantage. The Thunder, meanwhile, are dealing with a slew of injuries to key players, including Alex Caruso, Jaylin Williams, and Chet Holmgren, which has tested their depth. While both Antetokounmpo and Gilgeous-Alexander are playing at an All-NBA level this season, the Heat will need to rally together in Giannis’s absence. With the stakes high, Miami aims to secure a victory and keep pace in the competitive East. Fans will be eagerly watching to see how the Heat adapt and who steps up in this pivotal matchup.

item.description: FEATURE | Five things we learned from Bundesliga Matchday 10 The Bundesliga returned following the final international break of the year, and what a spectacle it was. From a swing of the title race pendulum, to changes at the bottom of the table, Get German Football News has you covered with the latest talking points after Matchday 10. Here are five things we learned… Bayern Munich have an attacking problem This would seem like an obvious thing to say after Harry Kane was ruled out for the next three months with an ankle injury,, while Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry are also out injured, but this has been a problem for most of the season too, and these injuries are likely to make the matter worse. Even with Kane fit, Bayern have been wasteful in front of goal this season. Granted, some of the results the ball just wouldn’t go in, like against Schalke and Augsburg, but the difference between this season and last year was that Bayern would prove to be far more clinical in front of goal, but Germany’s record champions seemed to have lost that edge now, as shown in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday night. This has resulted in games where Bayern should win comfortably being a lot more difficult, mainly due to their own doing. With the injury to Kane, and with no fit back-up, this problem is likely to get worse and could make or break Bayern’s Bundesliga season. It’s now up to Vincent Kompany and his coaching team to find a solution, and quick. Borussia Dortmund show some bottle Usually after Bayern drop points, Dortmund fail to capitalise, and ultimately, nothing would change. However, Matchday 10 was different. But a win is a win, and Dortmund are now top of the Bundesliga with a two-point lead over Bayern. item.title: Studs and duds from Bears' 21-13 win against the Saints
item.description: The Chicago Bears have now won five straight games after taking down the New Orleans Saints, 21-13, in Week 11. They still had two turnovers in this game, although they also forced two takeaways and scored 13 points off of them. Jeffery Simmons had one of the best games of his career, while Montez Sweat also had the Bears ’ first safety in nearly five years. Offensively, things stalled after the second quarter. Still, quarterback Caleb Williams finished the game with two touchdowns and completed over 65 percent of his passes. Chicago also got Salvon Ahmed involved in the running game and he finished with 33 rushing yards on just six carries. Here are mostly studs and a few duds from the Bears’ win against the Saints, including All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who tied his career-high in sacks in this game with three, and cornerback Jaylon Johnson, who once again struggled in coverage. Stud: DT Jeffery Simmons What a game for Jeffery Simmons. Throughout his career, he has always played well when facing New Orleans, but this was one of the best games of his entire career. Simmons tied his career-high in sacks with three. His only other game with three sacks was back in 2021. He now has five sacks in three games since joining the Bears. This trade has immediately paid off for Chicago and turned them into a championship-caliber defense. Dud: CB Jaylon Johnson After having a pick-six in Chicago’s last game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Jaylon Johnson returned to his regular-season form in this game. It felt like every time there was a blown coverage in this game, mostly against Chris Olave, Johnson was the one in coverage. The Bears’ weakness on defense is certainly their secondary and Johnson is a major reason why, since he is severely underperforming. Stud: WR Zavion Thomas This may have been the NFL’s introduction to Chicago’s rookie wide receiver, Zavion Thomas. His speed was on full display with his 30-yard run to set up the Bears’ second touchdown of the game and his impressive 40-yard catch on third-and-17 to set up Chicago’s field goal in the third quarter. However, his diving catch on a broken third-down play in the fourth quarter may have been his best play of the day, even though the Bears did not end up scoring on that drive. New Orleans’ secondary slowed down most of Chicago’s playmakers, but they could not stop Zavion Thomas. Dud: RB D’Andre Swift New Orleans clearly emphasized stopping the Bears from running the ball. item.title: ‘Worse outcome’ – Mike Pettine’s defense was worse than Christian Parker’s, says former Dallas Cowboys star
item.description: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Tennessee Titans to move to 5-6… But what about their defense? Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys’ offense stole the show against the Titans, winning 51-30. Ahead of the game, all the talk was about the team’s defense, after they promoted Mike Pettine to call plays in place of defensive coordinator Christian Parker. The switch was a response to the 46-40 loss to the 49ers, in which the Cowboys gave up almost 600 yards. Speaking after the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he was pleased with the way the defense played. He told his press conference: “Overall, I was very proud of the defensive unit, coaches, and everybody.” But his response did not please former Cowboys wide receiver Isaiah Stanback, who told the Cowboys’ postgame show that he felt the defense actually went backwards. He pointed to the fact the team gave up 30 points against a Titans team that is now 1-9 in the standings. Isaiah Stanback: Cowboys went backwards “I don’t wholly agree with him,” Stanback said, in response to Schottenheimer being proud of the Cowboys’ defense. He explained: “Last [week], he faced one of the more prominent offenses in the [offensive] play caller, and some of the most dangerous weapons in the NFL. He faced one of the better quarterbacks in the NFL, Brock Purdy. “Christian McCaffrey, one of the best running backs you have played in the game, as far as catching the ball, running the ball. “You got five sacks against [a] San Francisco 49ers outfit. You got five sacks against the Tennessee outfit that has Cam Ward, has Tony Pollard, Chimere Dike, that’s a big difference, right? “You gave up 46 last week. You gave up 30 to a Tennessee Titans team, that came in averaging 18 points per game. “So you can feel as if you performed better, but in reality, if I’m looking at it in totality, yes, you gave up more yards. Yes, you gave up bigger plays. All that stuff last week, but it was against a substantially better outfit. “So, to me, as I look at this, I think giving up 30 to this outfit is actually a worse outcome than even what you faced last [week], in my opinion.” The Cowboys’ defense will be tested next against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, who secured a surprise 19-16 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. item.title: Houston Dynamo midfielder Héctor Herrera charged with DWI in Montgomery County
item.description: Héctor Herrera on the pitch during a Houston Dynamo match in July. (Maria Lysaker/Getty Images) Houston Dynamo midfielder Héctor Herrera was charged with driving while intoxicated Saturday in Montgomery County, according to the sheriff's office. Herrera, 36, whom the team signed to a one-year deal in January, has bonded out of the Montgomery County Jail, according to Miranda Hahs, director of public affairs for the sheriff's office. Herrera's name did not appear in county court records or the jail inmate roster Sunday afternoon. Hahs did not answer further questions about the player's bail. No further information about the incident was available. The arrest comes days before the Dynamo are scheduled to begin the playoffs Tuesday in San Jose, Calif. The Tijuana, Mexico native was the Dynamo's highest paid player in 2022 with a salary of over $5 million. He's making $525,000 this year, according to the Football Reference online database. In a statement to the Chronicle, team communications manager Jack Holmes said the club and Major League Soccer are aware of Herrera's arrest. "The Houston Dynamo are aware of an incident involving Héctor Herrera on Friday night. The Club and Major League Soccer are working to gather additional information.We will refrain from providing further comment until appropriate," the statement read. item.title: It’s a Deal! Skubal to the Mets!
item.description: Sep 25, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) pitches during the first inning against the San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park. Mandatory Credit: Stan Szeto-Imagn Images It’s Official! Tarik Skubal is a New York Met . The New York Mets have agreed to terms with two-time AL Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal on a nine-year, $450 million contract , according to multiple reports on Sunday. The deal, first reported by the New York Post’s Jon Heyman and confirmed in its terms by ESPN’s Jeff Passan, sets a new standard as the richest contract ever given to a pitcher in MLB history. The agreement includes a $45 million signing bonus, full no-trade protection, and no opt-out clauses. Roughly $30 million is deferred. The average annual value comes to $50 million, also a record for a pitcher and well clear of the previous high-water marks set by Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander. It eclipses Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s 12-year, $325 million pact with the Dodgers by $125 million in total value. Skubal, who turned 30 last week, becomes the centerpiece of a Mets rotation that already features promising right-hander Nolan McLean. He joins a lineup built around Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette. For owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns, the signing is the clearest statement yet that the club intends to rebound from a disappointing 2026 season and contend immediately in 2027. The left-hander’s path to free agency was eventful. After winning consecutive Cy Young Awards in 2024 and 2025 with the Detroit Tigers, he underwent a procedure in May 2026 to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. He returned in roughly six weeks and was later traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers ahead of the deadline. Across both clubs in 2026, he went 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158⅔ innings. Because he changed teams midseason, the Dodgers could not make him a qualifying offer, so the Mets incur no draft-pick penalty for the signing. Skubal’s free-agent process moved quickly. He held in-person meetings last week in California with the Mets, Dodgers, Blue Jays, and Padres. New York was widely viewed as the favorite after an early offer in the neighborhood of nine years and nearly $400 million. Agent Scott Boras had indicated a strong likelihood the left-hander would decide before the collective bargaining agreement expires on December 1. Over the past three seasons, Skubal has posted a 2.42 ERA, ranking among the game’s elite in strikeouts, innings, and Wins Above Replacement. He has also shown postseason pedigree, with a career 2.13 ERA in eight playoff starts. The Mets are betting that version of Skubal remains the one who takes the mound in Queens for the rest of the decade.

item.title: Eagles vs. Steelers: The good, the bad, and the ugly
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Joe Milton III #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles passes the ball against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Steelers 19-16. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It looks like Nick Sirianni has his job for another week. It looks like the Eagles are heading towards a threepeat as NFC East champions, and another playoff run in 2026. Well, one of those statements may have a drop of truth to it after the Eagles snapped one streak and preserved another in a 19-16 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers on an overcast Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. The Eagles snapped their seven-game losing streak, their longest since 2012, during Andy Reid’s last season. The Eagles also continued their streak at home against Pittsburgh, winning for the 12th-straight time over the Steelers, who have not won in Philadelphia since October 24, 1965, (20–14 at Franklin Field), 61 years and two stadiums ago. Maybe the addition of former Eagles’ coach T.J. Paganatti as a consultant had something to do with the Eagles’ offensive line looking the best it has this season. The defense was strong, holding the Steelers to 73 yards rushing, 43 yards below their season average of 116 yards a game, and sacking 42-year-old relic Aaron Rodgers five times for minus-45 yards. Joe Milton was competent, moving the Eagles, especially in clutch situations, completing 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards. Saquon Barkley made a brief appearance as Saquon Barkley rushing for a game-high 75 yards, the bulk of which came on a first quarter 38-yard touchdown run, while Jeremiah Trotter Jr. led the defense with a game-high 13 tackles, Marcus Epps had his best game this season with a season-high 8 tackles, and a bunch of guys who had received very little playing time making significant contributions like Byron Young’s two sacks, Jon Jones’ three defended passes, and Gabe Hall coming off the practice squad for a sack. The Eagles are 3-7. But are they suddenly cured of the slopfest they perpetrated over the first nine games—absolutely not. More proof is demanded. If the Eagles can somehow beat Dallas, in Dallas, on Thanksgiving, with the lowly tanking Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts following them, this nightmare of a season could have life, with the Eagles sitting at 6-7 in an NFC East Division up for grabs. Did Sunday’s victory resuscitate the Eagles or briefly camouflage a bad football team for one week and in the long run hurt its draft status? The answer may be four days from now in Dallas. item.description: Chivas honoured the story of Antonio, a courageous Mexican A passion for sports, perseverance, and the desire to overcome any obstacle are some of the qualities that set Antonio Vázquez apart. The 17-year-old has turned every challenge into an opportunity to prove his abilities and achieve his goals. In recognition of his effort, hard work, and dedication, Club Deportivo Guadalajara invited him to enjoy an unforgettable experience at Estadio AKRON this Sunday, where he got to share his passion for the red and white up close. Originally from Mérida, Yucatán, Antonio was born with limb agenesis, a condition in which both his feet and his left hand are absent. When he was born, his parents were told he might never be able to walk. However, through tremendous effort, his family's support, and especially his grandmother's unconditional encouragement, he learned to do so and discovered one of his greatest passions in sports. He has played recreational soccer in local tournaments since he was 9, and for the past three years, he has represented Yucatán as a para-athlete in the 100 meters and shot put in the T42/F42 classifications. His dedication has already earned him gold medals in all his events at the state level, as well as standout performances at the CONADE National Paralympics. He has won four medals at this competition: a bronze in Oaxaca in 2024, a gold in the 100 meters in Aguascalientes in 2025, and two silvers—one in shot put in Aguascalientes in 2025 and another in the 100 meters at the 2026 edition held in Guadalajara, Jalisco. A red-and-white heart since 2017 Beyond his passion for sports, Antonio has a deep love for Guadalajara. item.title: No. 10 Iowa State falls at No. 4 Iowa
item.description: Iowa State’s Coby Merril wrestles Iowa’s Ben Kueter in a 285-pound match Nov. 22, 2026 during Cy-Hawk wrestling dual at Carver-Hawkeye Arena in Iowa City, Iowa. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co IOWA CITY — The Cyclones brought a halftime lead and a wave of momentum into Carver-Hawkeye Arena on Sunday. But when the No. 4 Hawkeyes needed a spark out of the break, their upper-middleweights delivered a decisive response. Behind a dramatic late takedown from Carter Schubert and back-to-back major decisions by Gabe Arnold and Angelo Ferrari, No. 4 Iowa stormed past No. 10 Iowa State 21-12 to reclaim the Dan Gable Traveling Trophy in the annual Iowa Corn Cy-Hawk Dual. The Hawkeyes jumped out to an early 7-0 dual advantage behind strong lower-weight performances. At 125 pounds, 16th-ranked Leo DeLuca opened the afternoon with a dominant 9-0 major decision over No. 29 Rin Sakamoto. Unranked Kale Peterson followed at 133 pounds, pulling off a 2-0 decision over No. 18 Garrett Grice using a second-period escape and a full third-period rideout. The 10th-ranked Cyclones answered with three straight victories from 141 to 157 pounds to take control before intermission. Fourth-ranked Evan Frost got Iowa State on the board at 141 with a 1-0 victory over No. 7 Nasir Bailey, controlling mat position after a second-period escape. His brother Jacob, followed at 149 with a 7-2 win over No. 6 Ryder Block, scoring two takedowns to avenge a loss from the 2022 high school state finals. No. 9 Paniro Johnson then scored a first-period takedown at 157 pounds to edge No. 18 Jordan Williams 4-3, giving Iowa State a 9-7 lead at the break. The dual swung back in Iowa’s favor immediately following intermission at 165 pounds. Locked in a tight battle with No. 17 Connor Euton, No. 9 ranked Carter Schubert executed a clutch takedown with less than 10 seconds remaining on the clock to snatch a 9-8 decision and put the Hawkeyes ahead 10-9. That late heroics opened the floodgates for Iowa’s middle lineup. At 174 pounds, fifth-ranked Gabe Arnold pushed a relentless pace against Tate Naaktgeboren to rack up a 17-6 major decision. Third-ranked freshman Angelo Ferrari kept the pressure on at 184 pounds, controlling Aiden Riggins in a 17-3 major decision that extended Iowa’s lead to 18-9 and put the dual out of reach. Iowa State chipped away at 197 pounds when No. 21 Brayden Thompson accumulated more than a minute of riding time to earn a 3-2 decision over No. 26 Harvey Ludington. However, top-ranked heavyweight Ben Kueter closed the door for the Hawkeyes, breaking a 1-1 tie in sudden-victory overtime with a sweep and takedown to cap a 4-1 decision over No. 12 Coby Merrill. With the victory, Iowa improves to 2-0 on the season, while Iowa State falls to 4-1. The Cyclones return to action Dec. 12–13 at the National Duals Invitational in Tulsa, Oklahoma. item.title: Billie Jean King Cup: Coco Gauff plays doubles, USA sweeps Hungary
item.description: DELRAY BEACH — Brandishing the American flag, Coco Gauff led her USA teammates around the court at Delray Beach Tennis Center. Then, still holding the flag, she danced with it to the rap music. After a late Saturday night that saw a 5 1/2-hour delay in her singles match, Gauff was back playing the key doubles match at 1:30 p.m. Sunday in a late switch by captain Lindsay Davenport . Though Coco rarely plays doubles anymore, she paired with lefty bomber Taylor Townsend , one of the world’s best doubles players and someone the 22-year-old Coco looked up to when she was a young teenager. More BJK Cup: Billie Jean King Cup plagued by thunderstorms, tornado watch It was a wonderful way to end it – two Black players with Palm Beach County roots, one the star of the singles tour, the other the star of the doubles tour. Coco and Townsend shook off a rocky start to repel Hungary’s Anna Bondar and Dalma Galfi 6-4, 6-3 to give USA the clinching third point in the best-of-five Billie Jean Cup qualifier . “I’m glad we closed it out because I didn’t want to play another singles match,’’ Gauff said. “There was always the scenario we’d be up 2-0 and maybe play (doubles) and try to finish it. We were prepared to play with each other. Taylor and Lindsay were confident in my ability to play doubles and then play singles after (if necessary).’’ It wasn’t necessary, but things looked dicey early. In the first set, Coco-Townsend fell behind 3-1 before rallying to win the next 3 games for a 4-3 lead. Still, at 4-4, Coco faced a break point that could’ve put USA behind 5-4. But the pair rallied for a 5-4 lead and closed it out. The second set also was tight before a late surge that gave Townsend-Coco the win and the insurmountable 3-0 USA lead. “I was following her lead for the most part,’’ Coco said. “She is going to go down as one of the greats of the sport (in doubles). Don’t compare me to her. She’s so much better than me. I wasn’t nervous but I hadn’t played doubles in a long time. I was confident but I didn’t play well most of the match.’’ Townsend is coming off winning the season-ending doubles title last week at Indian Wells and also won the Miami Open, French Open and U.S. Open doubles titles. The 30-year-old Townsend bashed about 10 overhead smash winners into the crowd Sunday. “It’s her mentality and positivity to be able to uplift your partner when not playing well,’’ Gauff said of Townsend. “She serves well and has the best hands on tour in my opinion.’’ Coco has very fast hands at the net, too, and came up with superlative volleys. But she also made errors as doubles positioning is different than singles. The two didn’t practice together during the week. Townsend was slated to play with doubles specialist Desirae Krawczyk. “Our first four games was our practice,’’ Townsend quipped. item.title: Skubal agrees to nine-year $450 mln MLB deal with Mets: reports
item.description: Picher Tarik Skubal has reportedly agreed to a nine-year MLB deal worth $450 million with the New York Mets (Patrick McDermott) Tarik Skubal, a two-time Cy Young Award winner as Major League Baseball's top pitcher, has agreed to terms on a record nine-year deal worth $450 million with the New York Mets, according to multiple reports on Sunday. The 30-year-old American left-hander spent his first six seasons with the Detroit Tigers before joining the Los Angeles Dodgers in a trade last August, but he was unable to help the club lift a third consecutive World Series trophy. The $50 million (45.5 million euros) average annual value would make the deal a record for pitchers, surpassing the $43.3 million annual value of contracts for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander. Skubal's deal also would be the richest contract for any pitcher in MLB history, surpassing the mark of $325 million set when the Dodgers signed Japan's Yoshinobu Yamamoto to a 12-year deal in 2024. Skubal became only the 12th pitcher in MLB history to win back-to-back Cy Youngs when he captured the award in the American League in 2024 and 2025. He completed the AL triple crown in 2024, leading the league in wins with 18 and in earned-run average at 2.39 plus topping MLB in strikeouts with 228. Skubal, a unanimous Cy Young choice in 2024, also had the AL's lowest earned-run average in 2025 at 2.21 and struck out 241 batters over 195 1/3 innings to repeat. In 2026, he won an arbitration hearing and was awarded $32 million for the 2026 season, but the campaign was cut short in May when he had to undergo surgery for loose bodies in his elbow. He returned in July and after joining the Dodgers, Skubal went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts over 62 innings, then went 1-1 in the playoffs, where the Dodgers were eliminated by eventual champion Milwaukee. Skubal, considered the top free agent player available, made the agreement as MLB owners and the MLB Players Association stand deadlocked over how to divide profits with the December 1 deadline for a new deal fast approaching. If the sides cannot agree on terms for a new collective bargaining agreement, a lockout is expected next month. item.description: Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images DJ Moore caught a four-yard pass from Josh Allen to score Buffalo’s first touchdown of the game before leaving the field late in the second quarter, according to RotoBaller NFL . Trainers helped the wide receiver to the sideline after he went down on an Allen interception, but he did not stay out long. Following treatment at the medical tent, Moore proceeded to the locker room under his own power, RotoBaller reported. The injury scare happened during a critical moment when the Bills were trying to build momentum against the Miami Dolphins. Moore had already made five catches for 41 yards before the play that sent him to the ground. He was initially listed as questionable to return, which made every fan on the edge of their seat. But the team’s medical staff cleared him to go back into the game. A Quick Return to Action Moore did not waste any time getting back on the field once he was cleared by the trainers. He reentered the game and immediately made an impact with an 18-yard reception. This play showed that his knee was stable enough to handle the physical demands of the NFL. The fact that he could run and catch without limping is a huge relief for the Bills offense. Players often hesitate after a hard hit, especially one that looks as bad as Moore’s did on the replay. His ability to snap back into the game speaks to his toughness and the quality of the medical care he received. RotoBaller reported that he added this 18-yard catch after reentering, proving he was ready to contribute right away. The Bills needed Moore healthy to keep their passing game moving against a strong Miami defense. Losing their top receiver for the rest of the game would have forced Josh Allen to look elsewhere for targets. Instead, Allen found Moore again for the score and the long gain. His return ensures the Bills have their primary weapon for the second half of the matchup. The team can now plan their plays around his route running without worrying about his availability. It was a rough moment, but the outcome was positive for the home team. The final stats for Moore include the touchdown and the long catch after his return. item.title: Leaders Barcelona make impressive Villarreal comeback, Atletico triumph
item.description: Villarreal defender Pau Navarro's own goal handed Barcelona the three points in their La Liga win at Camp Nou (Josep LAGO) Spanish champions Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga. Barca edged clear of Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid, who had pulled level with them on Saturday after beating Celta Vigo. Later Sunday, Atletico Madrid won 3-0 away at Getafe to stay on the trail of Spain's top two after a defeat in their previous outing by Barca. Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and Barca winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty. However, the Catalan giants struck three times in an 11-minute spell in the second half to claim victory. Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez pulled Barca level before Pau Navarro's own goal gave them the three points. Barca have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clasico defeat by Real Madrid in October. "We suffered because we started the game badly, we let in two goals very early. I'll remember how the team reacted but we have to work to ensure this doesn't happen again," Barca midfielder Pedri told DAZN. Barcelona coach Hansi Flick hailed his team's comeback, something they have made a habit of during his reign. "We made two mistakes and they scored two times... but the reaction that we had was unbelievable," Flick told reporters. The hosts were caught snoozing in the early afternoon sunlight and Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute. Lopez gave the ball away with a careless pass and Canada international Buchanan produced a perfect sliced effort from distance. Two minutes later, Villarreal doubled their advantage when Oluwaseyi smashed an effort over Joan Garcia into the roof of the net. Flick's side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Yamal in the area, but the teenage winger dragged his penalty against the post and wide. - Quickfire treble - Barcelona quickly dragged themselves back into the match after the interval. Martin found the net in the 57th minute with a header from Pedri's cross. Four minutes later Lopez slammed home the second after being teed up by Yamal, and the third was quick to follow. A clever backheel pass by Yamal fed Eric Garcia, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro. Substitute Anthony Gordon was denied by Peter Gulacsi and then appealed for a penalty after a bump from Santi Comesana but went down too easily. Lopez, who had been substituted off, was sent off for dissent as Barca protested on the sidelines. Flick said although he was happy with refereeing in Spain generally, he disliked Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez. "We saw which referee was there and we expect it," said Flick. item.title: Why Dolphins’ Malik Washington Has 0 Catches in Diverse Role
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Malik Washington #6 of the Miami Dolphins takes the field to face the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) Getty The Miami Dolphins are using Malik Washington in some different roles in recent weeks. It may not be resulting in huge receiving numbers, particularly with Kyle McCord at quarterback, but Washington is still contributing. It’s just creating some fascinating offensive production for the Dolphins’ slot receiver, particularly for any fans who are expecting to see Washington piling up some receiving yards for a team that often finds itself behind in games. On Sunday in Week 11 against the Buffalo Bills, for example, Washington had two touches in the first half. Both were runs. He ran on a gadget play for minus-4 yards, but then he had his most fascinating usage yet. The Dolphins had a short-yardage situation, lined up in shotgun, had Washington aligned next to McCord — and simply handed Washington the ball off to run between the right guard and right tackle. They sprung him with a sizable hole, and Washington picked up 15 yards. Washington didn’t have any catches in the first half, though, despite two targets. This comes a week after Washington threw a touchdown for the Dolphins. He can do a little bit of everything. Why Malik Washington Doesn’t Have Catches There are a couple of reasons Washington isn’t catching the football. The most obvious one on Sunday? McCord is struggling. In the first half in Buffalo, McCord had just four completions — he was 4-for-11 for 23 yards and an interception. He had a completion to WR Caleb Douglas, as well as to RB Ollie Gordon, FB DJ Herman and TE Greg Dulcich. McCord threw incomplete twice to Washington and three times to Chris Bell. It’s just not an offense set up to be highly successful in the passing game. Second Half Outlook On Sunday specifically, it seems like Washington has a chance to do more in the second half. The Dolphins are down 20-6 at the intermission and get the ball to start the second half. That certainly seems like an opportunity on the table for Washington to get some stats — assuming McCord can do something positive for Miami’s offense. McCord topped 200 yards passing last week, so he’s got at least some ability — and if the Bills’ lead gets even bigger, the Dolphins should have more room to complete some passes underneath, conceptually to Washington. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season.
